current_status.stage: Preclinical/formulation research; Phase 1 for lead obesity candidate targeted 2027
current_status.partner: None disclosed; company states it is pursuing a licensing/technology-export deal within 2026
current_status.data_point: DK-LADS is a microsphere-based DDS platform ('extends drug half-life, minimizes blood concentration fluctuations'); lead obesity candidate DKF-MB501 targets 3+ months of effect from a single injection

finding_history.summary: Dongkook detailed its microsphere-based DK-LADS drug-delivery platform, built on 30 years of in-house DDS work. Lead obesity candidate DKF-MB501 (single injection, 3+ months of effect) is in preclinical/formulation research with Phase 1 targeted for 2027; the article did not name semaglutide or tirzepatide specifically for DKF-MB501. Related DK-LADS-adjacent programs: Lorelin Depot (leuprolide) 1-month formulation launch targeted 2026, 3-month formulation targeted 2027; long-acting tacrolimus and octreotide (1- and 3-month) nearing clinical entry.

Dongkook Pharmaceutical is positioning its 30-year in-house DDS/DK-LADS expertise for a technology-licensing deal, with the company stating it is targeting a licensing agreement within 2026. A separate report (Korean-language) indicates the obesity candidate under DK-LADS is being developed with both semaglutide and tirzepatide under consideration, targeting monthly dosing with an eye toward extending to 3 months, and a Phase 1 entry goal of 2027.

Dongkook is building a dedicated ~₩60 billion sterile-injectable plant for microsphere/liposome products at its Jincheon (North Chungcheong) site, ~9,240 sqm, targeted to begin operating in H2 2027 — capacity infrastructure to support DK-LADS-based products including any semaglutide/tirzepatide LAI candidate. Exact announcement date approximate; sourced from a single trade-press report.
